transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess it’s mostly that I’ve been forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Nothing terrible, I hope, but it’s starting to bother me. Like I’ll miss a heart follow-up appointment, or forget to call the clinic back, or I’ll show up to do a repair and not have the right tools with me. I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you help with, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should come in.
Would you say this kind of forgetfulness is something new that started recently, or has it been a pattern for you since childhood or early adulthood?

I think it’s been there a long time, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even back in grade school I was kind of that kid who had trouble staying in his seat. I’d blurt things out, talk too much… teachers sent notes home about it sometimes. So, no, I don’t think it’s completely new.
Have you had any recent medical events—like a head injury, stroke, or significant illness—around the time these memory lapses became more noticeable?
Not that I can think of, no. I mean, I haven’t had anything like that happen around when I started noticing it more. At least nothing that stands out to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

These days, do you notice similar struggles—like trouble focusing, staying organized, or sitting still—in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, and in social situations, or is it really just the memory slips that stand out?

I guess it’s not just the memory slips, no. I mean, I try not to make a big thing of it, but it’s gotten to where the senior-center repair group can’t really count on me the way they used to. And my doctor’s office has had to chase me a bit about those heart follow-ups I missed. So… yes, I suppose it’s showing up in more than one place, if that makes sense.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, do you recall having trouble paying attention or sitting still that was noticeable enough to cause problems at school or at home?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible kid or anything, but in grade school I was definitely the one who had trouble staying in his seat. I’d call out answers before I was supposed to, talk too much, that sort of thing. Teachers did send notes home about it sometimes. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over the past several months, have you noticed feeling persistently down, low on energy, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think so, not in any steady way. I have my off days like anyone, and I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently down or lost interest in things. At least, nothing like that stands out to me. Is that what you mean?

Aside from these attention-related slips, have you noticed any new problems with your memory itself—like repeating questions, forgetting recent conversations, or getting confused about dates or places?

No, I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I misplace things or forget to follow through, sure, but I haven’t noticed myself repeating the same questions or getting lost about what day it is or where I am. At least, not that I’m aware of. My wife hasn’t said anything like that either… does that help?
Over the past several months, have you been feeling unusually anxious, tense, or worried much of the time?
No, I don’t think so… I mean, I worry about normal things, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious or tense much of the time. Nothing that feels unusual to me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Looking back over the years from childhood to now, would you say these attention and organization struggles have been fairly continuous, or was there a stretch—say in your 20s or 30s—when you felt this wasn't really a problem for you?

I think it’s been pretty continuous, yes… though I guess I always tried to think of it as just “how I was.” Even back in grade school, I was the kid who had trouble staying in his seat, talked too much, blurted things out before I should’ve… that sort of thing. I remember notes getting sent home about it. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but it’s not like there was some long stretch where it just disappeared.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since grade school, pre-age 12) symptoms of inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity (blurting out answers, difficulty remaining seated, talking excessively), with documented functional impact at school in childhood (notes sent home). These symptoms have persisted continuously into adulthood without a symptom-free interval, and currently cause impairment across multiple domains (missed medical appointments, unreliability in volunteer repair work). No evidence of acute cognitive decline, memory disorder (no repeated questions, disorientation, or recent-onset confusion), depressive episode, or anxiety disorder that could better explain the presentation. The chronic, early-onset, pervasive pattern of inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms with functional impairment supports a diagnosis of ADHD (ICD-10 F90.0), persisting into adulthood.
